CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Affinity & Identity Groups
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Status Affinity groups active in the Upper School[1]
Named in sources Black affinity group(s)[2]
Framework Diversity, Belongingness & Engagement (DBE)[3]
Named roster Not published publicly — see research note
What the sources confirm
Cannon names Affinity Groups as a flagship category of Upper School club life — grouping them among the
“significant” organizations in its club ecosystem. Independent reviews specifically reference Black affinity groups
and note that students can start new groups when their interests are not yet represented.[1,2]
The school connects this work to its stated commitment to Diversity, Belongingness, and Engagement (DBE),
describing a community where diverse perspectives are valued and everyone is meant to feel a sense of
belonging.[2,3]
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
This is the thinnest area for public data in the package. Cannon confirms affinity groups exist and are active (with Black
affinity groups named in reviews) and ties them to its DBE commitment — but it does not publish a named roster of
individual affinity/identity groups. To avoid fabrication, this dossier reports the confirmed structure and the one group
type named in sources, and does not invent a fuller list. A complete, named inventory would require direct confirmation
from the school.[1,2]

How Cannon frames Upper School club life
Cannon describes a “rich club life” in the Upper School that is student-led and faculty-supported, with clubs
meeting on a regular basis both during and after school hours. The stated purpose is to let students get involved
with what matters to them, voice their opinions, and learn from one another. The school explicitly highlights a range
from affinity groups, to interest clubs, to service clubs.[1]
A recurring theme across school and third-party sources is that students may start new clubs when their interests
are not already represented — so the active roster shifts year to year rather than being fixed.[1,5]
Named Upper School organizations surfaced in sources
The organizations below are those Cannon names directly on official pages or in its Upper School Deans’ Daily
Download. They illustrate the breadth of club life but are not a complete chartered list (see the research note).

belonging Groups dossier.[1]

(business)

Cannon School Esports Cross-division esports program with a dedicated lab; see Signature Competitive
Gaming (CSG) Programs.[5]
Two further families of Upper School organizations are documented in their own dossiers in this package:
discipline-based honor societies (Cum Laude, Mu Alpha Theta, Rho Kappa, and others) and signature
Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier Concord, North Carolina Page 1
competitive programs (robotics, esports, DECA, Model UN).
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
Cannon does not publish a centralized, chartered Upper School club directory. This catalog compiles every club
Cannon names on its own pages and Upper School blog, but the school’s student-initiated model means the live roster
changes annually and is not fully disclosed publicly. Treat this list as representative, not exhaustive — a precise club
count is not supportable from public sources.[1,5]

CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Governance & Student Leadership
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Student councils Lower, Middle & Upper School (all elected)[1,3,4]
Honor body Student-elected Honor Council[1]
Structure House System (advisory-based, 4-year)[1,2]
Club formation Student-initiated, faculty-sponsored[1,5]
Upper School Student Council
The Upper School Student Council leads community meetings and school-spirit events and reports activities to the
student body. Officers are President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and Public Relations Director; the
Executive Board comprises elected officers, class representatives, and faculty advisors.[1]
Honor Council & Honor Code
Honor is positioned as “a way of life.” Students sign an Honor Code and Unity Pledge each year — pledging to tell
the truth, respect others’ property, do their own work, and treat others with kindness and respect. A student-elected
Honor Council hears and adjudicates honor matters and is described by the school as a model of community
governance.[1,2]
The House System
Using advisory groups as its foundation, the House System provides leadership opportunities, peer tutoring,
community outreach, and social activities across all four Upper School years, building relationships between
students and adult advisors.[1,2]
Middle & Lower School leadership
The Middle School runs both a Student Council (grades 5–8, peer-elected) and an Advisory Council that plans the
division’s annual theme and activities. The Lower School operates its own elected Student Council focused on core
values and community.[3,4]
Club discovery & funding (folded in)
Cannon’s clubs are student-led and faculty-supported, and the consistent public signal is a student-initiated
founding model: students may create new clubs when their interests are not already represented. This is the
school’s primary discovery mechanism.[1,5]
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier Concord, North Carolina Page 1
Per the standing structure for this series, Funding and Discovery are folded into Governance here because public data
is thin. Cannon does not publish a formal club-chartering policy, an activities-fair process, or club budget/funding
details. The student-initiated, faculty-sponsored model is documented; financial and chartering specifics are not
disclosed and are not inferred here.[1,5]

School-wide academic honor
Cannon was awarded a chapter of the Cum Laude Society in 2005. Cum Laude recognizes scholastic
achievement and may elect up to 20% of the senior class in the college-preparatory curriculum.[1,2]
In 2025, students established Cannon’s first Science National Honor Society chapter — also the school’s first
student-run honor society — as a senior Capstone project, with an inaugural induction of 21 founding members.[3]

Editorial scope note
Three additional honor societies in Cannon’s slate — Tri-M Music Honor Society, the National Art Honor Society,
and the International Thespian Society — are arts-affiliated. By the series’ standing scope, arts programming has

CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Clubs & Activities — Lower School
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Division Lower School (JrK–Grade 4)
Leadership Lower School Student Council (elected)[1]
Signature program JrK / Senior Buddy program[1]
Enrichment After School Program (JrK–8) + Beyond the Bell[2]
Model Activity built around events, AE Days & enrichment[1]
How Lower School engagement works
Lower School student life is built less around standing interest-clubs and more around elected student leadership,
signature all-school traditions, Adaptive Expertise (AE) Days, and after-school enrichment. This is consistent with
how Cannon itself presents the division.[1]
Student leadership
The Lower School Student Council provides leadership opportunities and community connection, with elected
representatives and officers held to standards of academic integrity and conduct; responsibilities include
incorporating the school’s core values into year-long initiatives.[1]
Signature programs & traditions
• JrK / Senior Buddy program — pairs the youngest students with seniors for year-long mentorship and monthly
activities[1]
• Adaptive Expertise (AE) Days — interdisciplinary days featuring student-chosen “passion classes” such as
astronomy, cooking, woodworking, survival bracelets, and painting[1]
• Olympic Day — spring games with each class representing a country[1]
• Living History Museum — fourth-grade historical-figure presentations[1]
• Teddy Bear Picnic, Gold and Maroon Day, Family Picnic, and Grandparents / Special Friends Day[1]
After-school enrichment
Cannon’s After School Program serves students in junior kindergarten through eighth grade until 6:00 p.m. on an
as-needed basis, and the “Beyond the Bell” program offers enrichment options and private music lessons for an
additional charge.[2]
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier Concord, North Carolina Page 1
Lower School at Cannon does not operate a roster of standing interest-clubs in the way the Upper School does. The
student council, signature traditions, AE Days passion classes, and after-school enrichment above are what public
sources document for this division; this dossier reports that structure rather than implying a club catalog that does not
exist.[1]

CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Clubs & Activities — Middle School
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Division Middle School (Grades 5–8)
Meeting pattern During lunch or a designated club time[1]
Academic teams Battle of the Books, Science Olympiad, Model UN, Envirothon[1]
Student Council Grades 5–8, ~4 students per grade, elected[1]
Signature team Brainy Yaks robotics (grades 6–10)[3]
Overview
Middle School students at all grade levels can choose from clubs, academic competition teams, and enrichment
programs, with clubs scheduled during lunch or a designated club time so that student-athletes can also take part.
Additional clubs are created based on student interest, and Cannon’s “Beyond the Bell” program offers further
enrichment options.[1,2]
Academic competition teams
Cannon names the following faculty-facilitated academic competition teams in the Middle School:[1]
• Battle of the Books
• Elementary Battle of the Books
• Science Olympiad
• Model United Nations (Model UN)
• Envirothon
The Middle School also anchors Cannon’s flagship robotics team, the Brainy Yaks (members in grades 6–10),
covered in detail in the Signature Competitive Programs dossier.[3]
Student leadership & advisory
The Middle School Student Council draws from all four grades (5th–8th), typically about four students per grade,
elected by peers for a one-year term; duties include communicating news and events, planning social events, and
supporting student life. A separate Advisory Council helps faculty plan the annual Middle School theme and
organizes advisory activities.[1]
Signature advisory traditions include Pumpkin’ Chunkin’, the Big Wheel Derby/Relay, and the Doughnut Duel —
recurring “minute-to-win-it” style competitions that run across the year, plus community outings such as a Charlotte
Checkers game.[1]
Service teams
Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier Concord, North Carolina Page 1
A Middle School team coordinates volunteers for the Special Olympics of Cabarrus County, and the division runs a
broader service-learning program (detailed in the Service Learning & Community Engagement dossier).[1]
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
Cannon publishes its Middle School academic competition teams, student council, advisory council, and service teams
by name, but does not publish a complete list of interest-based MS clubs (which it says are formed by student interest).
The academic and leadership organizations above are confirmed; the broader interest-club roster is not centrally
enumerated.[1]

CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Service Learning & Community Engagement
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Annual service ~15,000 hours school-wide[1]
Requirement Service is not a graduation requirement[1]
Senior signature Capstone philanthropic projects[1]
US tradition House Day of Service[5,6]
Scale & philosophy
Cannon students collectively complete roughly 15,000 service hours each year through school-wide projects and
individual efforts. Notably, service is not a graduation requirement — the school frames this volume as a reflection
of student commitment rather than a mandate.[1]
Upper School
• Senior Capstones — philanthropic immersion projects culminating in presentations to faculty, staff, and
peers.[1]
• House Day of Service — a recurring Upper School service day organized through the House System.[5,6]
• Habitat Club and Winterm service trips (e.g., Sea Island Habitat for Humanity in South Carolina).[3,4]
Middle School service learning
Middle School service learning has students investigate topics of interest, identify needs in teams, and build action
plans. Documented partners and activities include the Special Olympics of Cabarrus County, the Society of St.
Andrew Gleaning Network, and the Cabarrus County Soil & Water Conservation District — with students
harvesting produce at a community garden, delivering canned food to the Salvation Army, and supporting a county
bilingual preschool.[2]
School-wide & seasonal efforts
Additional engagement surfaced in school communications includes blood drives and pediatric-cancer awareness
campaigns run through the Upper School.[6]

CANNON SCHOOL • CONCORD, NC • CLUBS & ACTIVITIES
Signature Competitive Programs
Inside Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier
AT A GLANCE
Flagship Brainy Yaks robotics (MS, grades 6–10)[1]
Robotics result Top 100 of 32,000+ teams, FLL Worlds (2024 & 2025)[1]
Esports Cannon School Gaming — dedicated lab since 2021[4]
Other teams DECA, Model UN, Science Olympiad, Envirothon[6,7]
Flagship: Brainy Yaks robotics
Cannon’s standout competitive program is the Brainy Yaks, a Middle School–anchored FIRST LEGO League
(FLL) robotics team whose members span grades 6–10. The team won the North Carolina FLL Champions Award
and advanced to the FLL World Championship in Houston, where it finished in the top 100 out of more than 32,000
teams worldwide — a result it reached in back-to-back years (2024 and 2025).[1,2]
The 2025 project focused on coral-reef restoration (“Reef Rescue”) under the FLL “Submerged” theme, developed
with input from a marine-biology mentor; the team also ranked among top competitors in innovation project, robot
design, and core values. The team’s coach — Cannon’s Director of Technology & Innovation — received one of
only four Coach/Mentor Awards across FIRST LEGO League.[1,3]
Note on framing: “top 100 of 32,000+” is the documented FLL standing. We report that result directly rather than
applying broader “elite/powerhouse” language.
Esports — Cannon School Gaming (CSG)
Cannon School Gaming launched in fall 2020 and now occupies a dedicated esports lab, converted from the
former media-production studio in summer 2021. Programming began with LAN parties and competition in Fortnite,
League of Legends, Rocket League, and Overwatch, and the school offers a related “The Business of Esports”
course. Esports is led by a Director of esports (role only; name omitted per series policy).[4,5]
Business & academic competition
• DECA — Upper School business competition; Cannon students reached finalist standing at the 2026 DECA
CDC in events including entrepreneurship, marketing, and personal financial literacy.[6]
• Model UN — the Upper School team attended the Duke (DUMUNC) conference among 400+ delegates, earning
Outstanding Delegate and Verbal Commendation recognitions.[6]
• Middle School academic teams — Science Olympiad, Envirothon, Battle of the Books, and Model UN.[7]
Supporting facilities
Competitive and maker programs are supported by three makerspaces (including “The Mill”), a Texas Grace Audio
Lab, and the dedicated esports lab.[5,8]
Cannon School — Clubs & Activities Research Dossier Concord, North Carolina Page 1
RESEARCH NOTE / GAP FLAG
Robotics is correctly classified as a FIRST LEGO League (FLL) program, not VEX — some aggregator pages refer only
to a generic “World Championship.” DECA and Model UN results are taken from the Upper School’s own daily blog and
reflect the most recent cycle surfaced; a full multi-year results history is not centrally published.[1,6]
